accessible_name: Inductive definition of formulas in the simplified first-order language
listen_text: Atomic clause: P of a and P of v sub i are formulas, for every natural-number index i. Negation clause: if A is a formula, then not A is a formula. Conjunction clause: if A and B are formulas, then the parenthesized conjunction A and B is a formula. Existential clause: if A is a formula and x is a variable, then there exists x such that A is a formula. Limiting clause: nothing else is a formula. The definition generates every formula from atomic formulas by repeated negation, conjunction, and existential quantification, and excludes all strings not generated by those clauses.
long_description: The definition generates every formula from atomic formulas by repeated negation, conjunction, and existential quantification, and excludes all strings not generated by those clauses.

Negation clause: if A is a formula, then not A is a formula.
Conjunction clause: if A and B are formulas, then the parenthesized conjunction A and B is a formula.
Existential clause: if A is a formula and x is a variable, then there exists x such that A is a formula.
Limiting clause: nothing else is a formula.

accessible_name: First-order axioms for a reflexive and transitive relation
listen_text: Reflexivity: for every v sub zero, P relates v sub zero to itself. Transitivity: for all v sub zero, v sub one, and v sub two, if P relates the first to the second and the second to the third, then P relates the first to the third. Together these two sentences say that the interpretation of the binary predicate P is a preorder on the domain of the structure.
long_description: Together these two sentences say that the interpretation of the binary predicate P is a preorder on the domain of the structure.
ordered_steps: Reflexivity: for every v sub zero, P relates v sub zero to itself.
Transitivity: for all v sub zero, v sub one, and v sub two, if P relates the first to the second and the second to the third, then P relates the first to the third.
